questions.question: In cricket, when a ball bowled as per rules passes the batsman without touching the bat or batsman and runs are scored on that ball, then those runs are considered as ____.
questions.questionHtml: In cricket, when a ball bowled as per rules passes the batsman without touching the bat or batsman and runs are scored on that ball, then those runs are considered as ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bye.
Key Points
  • Bye: A run is scored when the batsman does not touch the ball with either his bat or body. First recorded in the 1770s.

Additional InformationA glossary of cricket terms:

Terms Explanation
Leg-Before Wicket (LBW) It's a way to get the batter out. In other words, the hitter is out if the umpire determines that the ball struck any portion of the batter's body—typically the leg—prior to striking the bat or missing the bat and would have struck the stumps.
Maiden An over where no runs that are attributable to the bowler are scored (byes or leg-byes may be scored in this over, though, as these don't count against the bowler).
Wide Ball A delivery that pitches too far away from the batsman and so proves impossible to score off. The umpire will single this by stretching his arms out horizontally; an extra will be added to the total and the ball will be bowled again.
Bouncer A short-pitched ball which passes the batsman at chest or head height
Chinaman A ball bowled by a left-arm slow bowler that turns into the right-hand batsman, in effect a left-arm legspinner. Named after Puss Achong.
Mankad A term popular mainly in indoor cricket - but also fairly popular in Australia for outdoor cricket. Mankad is when the bowler brings his arm around and, instead of releasing the ball, runs out the non-striker by whipping off the bails. This type of dismissal is rare - and usually a warning is given to the batsman beforehand. Named after Vinod Mankad, who twice dismissed Australian Bill Brown this way.
Doosra A Hindi/Urdu word which means "second" or "other", the doosra is the offspinner's version of the googly, delivered out of the back of the hand and turning away from the right-hand batsman.

questions.question: Who had proposed the motto of Olympics ?
questions.questionHtml: Who had proposed the motto of Olympics ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pierre de Coubertin.

Key Points

  • Olympic motto comprises of three Latin word-
    • Citius (Faster) 
    • Altius (Higher)
    • Fortius (Stronger)
  • These words were first used by Dominican Priest Henri Didon.
  • He used it at the opening ceremony of school sports days. 
  • Pierre de Coubertin was also present at that ceremony. Later he prosed this as the Olympic motto.

Additional Information

  • Since Pierre de Coubertin revived the games, he is also known as the Father of Modern Olympic Games.
    • He was the second President and also the founder of the International Olympic Committee.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to basketball?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to basketball?

options.text: Each team is made up of 11 players, with only 7 allowed on the court at any time.
options.html: Each team is made up of 11 players, with only 7 allowed on the court at any time.

options.text: Each team is made up of 12 players, with only 5 allowed on the court at any time.
options.html: Each team is made up of 12 players, with only 5 allowed on the court at any time.

options.text: Each team is made up of 11 players, with only 4 allowed on the court at any time.
options.html: Each team is made up of 11 players, with only 4 allowed on the court at any time.

options.text: Each team is made up of 12 players, with only 8 allowed on the court at any time.
options.html: Each team is made up of 12 players, with only 8 allowed on the court at any time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Each team is made up of 12 players, with only 5 allowed on the court at any time. Key Points

  • In basketball, each team typically has 12 players on the roster, including substitutes.
  • At any given time, 5 players from each team are allowed on the court to play.
  • Substitutions can be made throughout the game as per the rules.
  • There is no limit to the number of substitutions a team can make during a game.

Additional InformationThe 5 players on the court typically have specific roles:

  • Point Guard (PG): The primary ball-handler and playmaker.
  • Shooting Guard (SG): A strong shooter, often tasked with scoring points from mid-range and three-point shots.
  • Small Forward (SF): A versatile player who can score, defend, and assist.
  • Power Forward (PF): Focuses on rebounding, defending, and scoring close to the basket.
  • Center (C): Usually the tallest player, specializes in shot-blocking, rebounding, and scoring in the paint.

questions.question: The terms Kumi-Kata, Shintai, Ukemi are associated with which sports?
questions.questionHtml: The terms Kumi-Kata, Shintai, Ukemi are associated with which sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Judo.

Key Points

  • Judo:-
    • Judo is a Japanese martial art that originated in the late 19th century.
    • It was developed by Jigoro Kano, who was a practitioner of Ju-jitsu, a traditional Japanese martial art.
    • Ju-jitsu is a close-combat fighting system that originated in feudal Japan and was used by the samurai.
    • Judo is based on the principles of Ju-jitsu but emphasizes throws, pins, and joint locks rather than strikes and kicks.
    • Judo became an Olympic sport in 1964 and is now practiced worldwide.
    • The terms Kumi-Kata, Shintai, Ukemi are associated with Judo.

Additional Information

  • Polo
    • Polo, game played on horseback between two teams of four players each of who uses mallets with long, flexible handles to drive a wooden ball down a grass field and between two goalposts.
    • It is the oldest of equestrian sports.
    • A game of Central Asian origin, polo was first played in Persia (Iran) at dates given from the 6th century BC to the 1st century AD.
  • Fencing:-
    • It is an intriguing sport with roots dating back centuries.
    • It originated as a form of sword fighting among European nobility, and over time, it has evolved into a competitive sport that tests physical fitness, speed, agility, and strategic thinking.
  • Wrestling:-
    • Wrestling is a popular sport in India and has a rich history.
    • It is believed to have originated in the Indus Valley Civilization around 5000 years ago.
    • India has produced many legendary wrestlers in the past, including the likes of Dara Singh, Sushil Kumar, and Yogeshwar Dutt.

questions.question: How many minutes is the duration of a Kabaddi match?
questions.questionHtml: How many minutes is the duration of a Kabaddi match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 40 minutes.
Key Points
  • Kabaddi is a popular contact sport in South Asia.
  • It is played between two teams of 7 players each.
  • The objective of the game is for a player, known as a raider, to cross into the opposing team's half and tag as many defenders as possible before returning to their own half.
  • A match consists of two halves, each lasting 20 minutes (total 40 minutes), with a break of 5 minutes in between.
  • Kabaddi is also known as hu-tu-tu in western India, ha-do-do in eastern India and Bangladesh, chedu-gudu in southern India, gudu in Sri Lanka, and theechub in Thailand.

Boxing 4 to 12 rounds of 3 minutes each.

questions.question: What is the duration of the interval in a football match?
questions.questionHtml: What is the duration of the interval in a football match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 15 minutes.

Key Points

  • Players are entitled to an interval at half-time, not exceeding 15 minutes; a short drinks break (which should not exceed one minute) is permitted at the interval of half-time in extra time.
  • Competition rules must state the duration of the half-time interval and it may be altered only with the referee’s permission.
  • A match lasts for two equal halves of 45 minutes which may only be reduced if agreed between the referee and the two teams before the start of the match and is in accordance with competition rules.

Additional Information

  • Football in India has historically been among the top 3 most popular sport in terms of players participation and TV viewership, together with long time number one cricket and re-emerging kabaddi.
  • India's current top domestic football league is Indian Super League, formed with eight teams to promote Indian football in the country and world. 
  • Also contested is Santosh Trophy, a knock-out competition between states (provinces) and government institutions.
  • The India national football team is the national football team of India and is governed by the All India Football Federation.

questions.question: Which international organisation is the current governing body of Badminton?

questions.solution:

questions.question: When were female participants formally admitted to the Olympic Games?
questions.questionHtml: When were female participants formally admitted to the Olympic Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Paris, 1900

Key Points

  • 1900 was the year when women first participated in the Modern Olympics.
  • The 1900 Summer Olympics, held in Paris, France, marked the first time women were allowed to compete.
  • Women participated in events such as tennis, sailing, croquet, equestrian, and golf.
  • This was a significant milestone in the history of the Olympic Games, promoting gender equality in sports.

Additional Information

  • Athens was the venue for the first Olympics which was held in 1896.
    • Since then Games are held every four years.
  • The Olympic flag was created in 1913 at the suggestion of Baron Pierre de Coubertin.
  • In the Amsterdam Games in 1928, an Olympic flame was ceremonially lighted and burned in a giant torch at the entrance of the stadium. 
  • The Olympic motto is “Citius Altius Fortius” (faster, higher, stronger).
  • The Modern Olympics were revived in 1896, but women were not allowed to compete in that year.
  • Over the years, the inclusion of women in the Olympics has grown, with more events and opportunities for female athletes.
  • Today, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) strives for gender parity in the Olympic Games.
  • The inclusion of women in the Olympics has had a lasting impact on promoting women's sports and inspiring future generations of female athletes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Grand Slam in Tennis?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a Grand Slam in Tennis?
questions.solution:
Option 2 is correct, Indian Open.

  • The 4 biggest tournaments in tennis are called Grand slams.
    • The Grand Slam tournaments are the four most important annual tennis events. The tournaments are - Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon, and the US Open.
    • The first of the Grand Slams was Wimbledon in 1877, followed by the US Open in 1881, the French Open in 1891 and the Australian Open in 1905.
    • All four Grand Slams have been played every year since inception in 1905, with the exception of the First and Second World Wars and the 1986 Australian Open.
    • The Australian Open is the first Grand Slam of the year (January), followed by the French Open (May-June), Wimbledon (June-July) and the US Open (August-September).
    • Both the Australian Open and US Open are played on hard courts, while the French Open is played on clay and Wimbledon is played on grass.
    • These four Grand Slam tournaments are the most important tennis events of the year in terms of world ranking points, tradition, prize-money.
  • Note-
    • Mahesh Shrinivas Bhupathi is a retired Indian professional tennis player. In 1997, he became the first Indian to win a Grand Slam tournament with Rika Hiraki.
    • French Open tennis tournament often referred to as 'Roland Garros' is held every year at the Stade Roland-Garros in Paris, France.

questions.question: The length of the men's kabaddi court is _____ metres.
questions.questionHtml: The length of the men's kabaddi court is _____ metres.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 13 metres

Key Points

  • The length of the men's kabaddi court is 13 metres.
  • The standard dimensions for a kabaddi court for men are 13 meters in length and 10 meters in width.
  • The kabaddi court is divided into two equal halves, each occupied by one team during the match.
  • The game is played with 7 players on each side, and the objective is to score points by raiding the opponent's half and touching as many of their players as possible without getting caught.
  • Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in India and is popular in various countries across South Asia.

Additional Information

  • The standard dimensions for a women's kabaddi court are slightly smaller, measuring 12 meters in length and 8 meters in width.
  • Kabaddi is governed internationally by the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF), which sets the rules and regulations for the sport.
  • The game is also featured in various international multi-sport events, including the Asian Games.
  • Kabaddi is known for its unique blend of physical strength, strategy, and agility, making it an exciting and dynamic sport to watch and play.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the game of Kho Kho ?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the game of Kho Kho ?

options.text: Ten players take the field in the beginning to start the match
options.html: Ten players take the field in the beginning to start the match

options.text: It is one of the oldest traditional tag games of India
options.html: It is one of the oldest traditional tag games of India

options.text: Three defenders of opposite team try to avoid being touched by the chasers
options.html: Three defenders of opposite team try to avoid being touched by the chasers

questions.solution:
Option 1 is incorrect.

Key Points

  • Kho-kho, a traditional Indian sport, a form of tag that is one of the oldest forms of outdoor sport. Hence, it is one of India's oldest traditional tag games.
  • A team consists of 12 players, one coach, one manager, and other supporting staff. 9 players will take the field at the beginning to start the match. Hence Only 9 Players take the field at the beginning to start the match.
  • 3 defenders of the opposite team try to avoid being touched by the chasers. Hence Three defenders of the opposite team try to avoid being touched by the chasers.
  • It is a high energy game that involves running and chasing.
  • The motive of the sitting team is to "tag" the opponents. Hence It is one of the oldest traditional tag games in India.
  • The chasers can run only in one direction and cannot cross the central lane. They have to run around the post to reach another side.
  • The other option is to pass the chasing job to another chaser whose back is facing you as you are running.
  • The attacker touches the chaser he wants (usually nearest to the target) and utters the word “Kho" loudly to signify the change.

questions.question: Where did the indigenous sport ‘Gatka’ originate from?
questions.questionHtml: Where did the indigenous sport ‘Gatka’ originate from?
questions.solution: Gatka is a traditional martial art form originating from Punjab, associated with the Sikh community and dating back to the times of the Sikh Gurus. It involves the use of weapons like swords, sticks, and shields, performed as both a sport and self-defense. Known for its graceful movements, agility, and quick reflexes, Gatka is showcased during Sikh festivals such as Hola Mohalla and Gurpurabs.

questions.question: A handball match lasts for a total of _______ minutes.

questions.solution: Handball, or team handball, is an indoor sport played between two teams of seven players (six outfield players and a goalkeeper) on a 40m x 20m court. questions.question: In which of the following games is the 'Baulk Line' used?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following games is the 'Baulk Line' used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kabaddi.

Key Points

  • The 'Baulk Line' is a critical feature in the game of Kabaddi.
  • It is used to determine the playing area for raiders and defenders.
  • A raider must cross the baulk line to make their raid valid.
  • Crossing the baulk line puts pressure on the defenders and adds a strategic element to the game.

Additional Information

  • Kabaddi
    • Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in India.
    • The objective of the game is for a single player, known as a "raider," to run into the opposing team's half of the court, tag out as many of their defenders as possible, and return to their own half of the court, all without being tackled by the defenders, and in a single breath.
    • The baulk line plays a critical role during a raid. A raider must cross this line to make their raid valid, and it acts as a challenge for both raiders and defenders.
    • Kabaddi has gained international recognition and is played in several countries, with professional leagues and tournaments being organized globally.
  • Badminton
    • Badminton is a racquet sport played using racquets to hit a shuttlecock across a net.
    • It is usually played as a singles or doubles game.
    • The boundaries of the playing area in badminton are defined by lines on the court, but terms like "baulk line" are not used in this sport.
  • Tennis
    • Tennis is a racquet sport that can be played individually against a single opponent (singles) or between two teams of two players each (doubles).
    • The court is rectangular and bounded by lines, but does not include a "baulk line."
    • Players use the tennis racquet to hit the ball over a net into the opponent's court.
  • Kho-Kho
    • Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian sport that involves two teams of twelve players each.
    • The game is played on a rectangular field, and the main objective is to avoid being tagged by members of the opposing team.
    • While the sport involves various lines and zones, such as the central line and the posts, the term "baulk line" is not applicable to Kho-Kho.
